summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer, and hypertension was admitted for intractable nausea and vomiting. She developed respiratory depression after receiving 1 mg IV Ativan in the ED, requiring ICU monitoring, but recovered within 24 hours. She also experienced hypertensive urgency with BP up to 215/140, managed with IV labetalol and hydralazine, and presented with a single episode of hematemesis likely due to a Mallory-Weiss tear, prompting temporary discontinuation of aspirin and initiation of twice-daily PPI therapy. Her blood glucose was elevated on admission, raising concern for DKA, but was managed with increased insulin coverage without needing an insulin drip. She was treated with IV fluids, antiemetics including ondansetron, Reglan, and IV erythromycin, and advanced to a regular diet. She was discharged home in stable condition tolerating oral intake, with instructions to avoid high-dose benzodiazepines, follow up with GI for pacer interrogation and erythromycin evaluation, and continue home medications including adjusted lisinopril and insulin regimen.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
